article.name: Aeris
article.summary: Aeris is described as a deterministic cognitive simulation engine. Memory models and retrieval are specified in documentation, while the reviewed repository tree contains no engine implementation; documented designs are not runtime evidence.

who_what.text: GitHub identifies Cedrick-Coto as the public repository owner. The README describes Aeris as a deterministic cognitive simulation engine for a Pokémon world, not a conversational memory service. This assessment is limited to repository documentation and tree state at the pinned revision.

architecture.text: Documented design: the README separates an ECS simulation from cognition, affect, and narrative. docs/03-data-models.md defines MemoryData with type, description, emotional weight, certainty, importance, simulation timestamp, location and involved-entity references, category, and tags. BeliefData includes confidence, source, times, supporting/contradicting memory IDs, and status. These described data records were not found as runtime types in the reviewed source tree.

The persistence document gives SQLite/JSON configuration and sample migration, backup, restore, and export designs. The only file under src/Aeris.Engine in the reviewed tree is its project file, so those examples do not establish implemented persistence or durability.

behavior.text: Retrieval (documented contract): a MemoryRetrievalSystem orchestrator reads long-term memory, working-memory context, and affect; a replaceable strategy returns scored memories and activation boosts; the orchestrator is described as loading selections into working memory and recording a separate causal trace. The proposed LinearScan filters forgotten/low-importance entries, applies an effective-importance threshold, scores importance/recency/context overlap/attention, stable-sorts, and applies top-N. Activation-based and embedding-based strategies are marked future. This is a contract description, not observed runtime behavior.

Write and correction: inspected data-model and retrieval documents do not specify an implemented write API, update/correction history, or stale-value resolution. The behavior is unknown at this revision.

Deletion: the retrieval contract says forgotten memories are excluded from candidates. The reviewed documents and source tree do not establish a deletion API, erasure, or lifecycle propagation; deletion behavior is unknown.

Scope: documented records contain entity/location references, but the inspected retrieval contract defines no tenant/principal authorization boundary. These fields do not establish security isolation.

Provenance and evidence: data-model documentation distinguishes observed, experienced, learned, inferred, and forgotten memories and gives beliefs source and supporting/contradicting memory IDs. The retrieval contract proposes a trace with outcome, factor values, score, and strategy. These are documented structures; implementation, external citations, and claim-level evidence support remain unverified.

metrics.evidence: Documented scenarios specify desired relevant recall and empty results; no Aeris runtime responses were captured or adjudicated.
No implemented correction/history path or post-correction probes were established by this source review.
The contract filters Forgotten candidates, but deletion acceptance and post-delete behavior were not established or probed.
No tenant/principal boundary was found in the inspected memory contract and no cross-scope probes ran.
The contract proposes computational retrieval trace fields, but no generated claims or citations were captured and adjudicated.
The contract gives O(L log L) complexity for its proposed baseline; this is not a runtime measurement. No latency or write-to-recall observations exist.
Documentation examples do not provide Aeris workload usage, cost, or storage measurements.
No runtime instrumentation path was established in the inspected documentation/engine project tree; no latency distribution was recorded.

limits.text: This is a documentation and repository-tree review. The README marks memory retrieval in progress and the reviewed engine source directory contains only a project file. Detailed designs and scenarios must not be read as implemented behavior or passing validation.

The review does not establish runtime correctness, persistence, correction, deletion completeness, tenant isolation, evidence quality, latency, or production reliability. Unknown means not verified here, not a claim that future work cannot implement the behavior.

benchmark.text: Status: Benchmark not run for Aeris. The project execution-status record states no metric values or execution observations were produced; fixture probe counts are planned only. No Aeris workload or test suite was run for this review.
